tldr_label: TL;DR — Alphabet suffers its worst day on record, Lagarde announces an early exit, and Iran weighs its reply to Vance

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: Alphabet fell 12.6%, which outlets called its worst day on record, and the Nasdaq lost 1.4%. Amazon dropped after hours, and Tokyo and Seoul slid on Friday. [[TAG:danger:Alphabet -12.6%]]

tldr_bullets.label: Central banks
tldr_bullets.body: The ECB held at 2.5% as Christine Lagarde announced she will leave in February 2027. The Bank of Japan held at 1.25% and signaled a possible December hike.

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Iran says it is drafting a reply to Vance's letter. It also claims tankers struck mines in Hormuz, which has not been verified, while officials say US military options are being prepared. [[TAG:warning:unverified claims]]

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: The full count leaves Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats, Eisenkot's at 48 and Arab parties at 19. Herzog is expected to begin consultations on November 4.

tldr_bullets.label: Spain
tldr_bullets.body: The toll from the Urda crash stands at 69. The transport minister says investigators are examining an 'inexplicable' order from a control center.

tldr_bullets.label: US
tldr_bullets.body: Third-quarter GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate. With four days left before the midterms, Democrats lead the final polls and Trump has canceled two rallies.

sections.title: AI Sell-off
sections.summary: Alphabet's record drop drags down the Nasdaq; Amazon slides after hours and Asia follows

paragraphs.heading: Alphabet's worst day
paragraphs.body: The Detroit News reported that Alphabet was on track for a record loss as its results revived fears about AI spending. KRMG reported that the S&P 500 fell 0.3% to 7,720.39. Yahoo Finance said the Nasdaq led the indexes lower, and StockTitan put the Nasdaq's loss at 1.38% to 26,184.72. Most S&P 500 stocks rose, so the decline was concentrated in a few large names. [[TAG:danger:Nasdaq -1.4%]]

paragraphs.heading: Amazon
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Amazon's third-quarter results came in below expectations, and the Motley Fool said the shares fell on concerns about capital spending. Reports put the after-hours drop at about 6%. AWS growth was strong, but free cash flow was negative. 24/7 Wall St. said Meta rose about 3% during the day while its rivals fell.

paragraphs.heading: Asia Friday
paragraphs.body: The Market Reporter said Asian markets slid in an AI sell-off on Friday, with Japan's Nikkei and Korea's Kospi among the hardest hit. Reported figures vary by timestamp, but the Kospi fell between 4% and 5% and Hong Kong rose. [[TAG:warning:figures vary]]

sections.title: Central Banks and Growth
sections.summary: ECB holds at 2.5% as Lagarde announces an early exit; BoJ eyes December; US GDP grows 3.4%

paragraphs.heading: ECB and Lagarde
paragraphs.body: Euronews reported that the ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5%, with inflation at 3.8%, close to double its target. President Christine Lagarde announced that she will leave early, in February 2027. Bloomberg said her departure adds to alarm over oil prices and stress in the French bond market. The Irish Times reported that the bank paused its rate hikes. [[TAG:warning:Lagarde exit]]

paragraphs.heading: Bank of Japan
paragraphs.body: Bloomberg reported that the BoJ held its benchmark rate after a hike in September. GuruFocus said the bank signaled a possible hike in December. KuCoin reported an 8-1 vote, with one board member pushing for 1.5%.

paragraphs.heading: US economy
paragraphs.body: The Bureau of Economic Analysis said real GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, led by investment and consumer spending. The Lane Report put the figure at 3.4% as well. Some outlets reported different inflation readings within the report, so this briefing does not cite one. [[TAG:success:GDP +3.4%]]

sections.title: Iran on the Brink
sections.summary: Tehran drafts a reply to Vance, claims tankers hit mines, and the US readies military options

paragraphs.heading: The Vance letter
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera, citing the New York Times, reported that Vance's letter to Mohsen Rezaei proposed early talks led by Vance and required Iran's nuclear program to be on the table. The Washington Times reported that Iran says it is drafting a response. Trump has said the outreach concerned humanitarian supplies, and Al Jazeera said he warned Gulf states to 'prepare'. Fox News, citing officials, reported that military options are being readied for the president before the midterms. [[TAG:danger:strikes possible]]

paragraphs.heading: Hormuz
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Iran says four tankers struck mines in Hormuz. WISH-TV reported three. The claims have not been independently verified, and the US says the main routes have been cleared. Gulf News said the UK maritime agency UKMTO confirmed a separate attack on a tanker off Oman. Oilprice.com reported that prices had fallen earlier on the Vance outreach, and FinanceFeeds put Brent near $114 on Thursday.

sections.title: Israel's Stalemate
sections.summary: The final count confirms no majority; Herzog is expected to start consultations on November 4

paragraphs.heading: Final count
paragraphs.body: NBC News reported that the final results show neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot can immediately form a government: 53 seats for Netanyahu's bloc, 48 for Eisenkot's and 19 for the Arab-led parties. NPR described the result as a stalemate. The results still need to be certified and presented to President Herzog. [[TAG:warning:no majority]]

paragraphs.heading: What comes next
paragraphs.body: Ynet explained that the president consults every faction and then assigns the task of forming a government. Consultations are expected to begin on November 4. TRT World reported that Herzog urged parties to avoid another election. He may push for a unity government, but Eisenkot has rejected serving under Netanyahu.

sections.sources: NBC News, NPR, Ynet, TRT World

sections.title: Russia's Two Fronts
sections.summary: Dnipro station toll rises to 14 as the Moscow summit closes with pledges to Africa

paragraphs.heading: Dnipro
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that at least 14 people were killed in the Russian attack on Dnipro's main train station and that Russian strikes killed at least 19 people across Ukraine that day. Russia said it shot down most of the more than 600 drones launched toward Moscow overnight. [[TAG:danger:14 killed]]

paragraphs.heading: Russia-Africa summit
paragraphs.body: The Kremlin said the third Russia-Africa summit ended with a final declaration, a declaration on cooperation in artificial intelligence, and an action plan for 2027 to 2029. Fortune reported that Putin called Africa a 'natural ally'. Accounts differ on attendance, giving 21 or 22 African leaders, and on how many deals were finally signed.

sections.title: Europe
sections.summary: Spain probes an 'inexplicable' rail order as the toll hits 69; EU and Canada balk at a label

paragraphs.heading: Urda crash
paragraphs.body: Euronews and Time reported that the death toll from Wednesday's high-speed crash was revised to 69 after the Transport Ministry briefly reported 74. ABC News said Transport Minister Óscar Puente pointed to an 'inexplicable' order from a central control center that let one train proceed toward a stopped train. The Boston Globe noted that the crash comes ahead of Spain's national election. [[TAG:danger:69 dead]]

paragraphs.heading: EU-Canada summit
paragraphs.body: BNN Bloomberg reported that Carney and Ursula von der Leyen floated 'associate member' status for Canada in Montreal. CBC reported on the debate over the label. Reports say Germany, France and others resisted it, and the draft joint statement dropped it. The final joint statement had not been published at the time of these reports.

sections.title: Africa
sections.summary: US sanctions Rwanda's defense ministry over M23; Darfur market strike toll disputed

paragraphs.heading: Rwanda sanctions
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post and ABC News reported that the US sanctioned Rwanda's defense ministry over its support for M23 rebels in eastern Congo. US News said the Treasury also targeted a financial institution that serves the security services. Rwanda denies backing the rebels.

paragraphs.heading: Darfur
paragraphs.body: NBC News reported that a Sudanese rights group says more than 100 people were killed in an army drone strike on a market in Nyala earlier this week. Doctors Without Borders gave a lower count of at least 36, according to Daily Sabah, and Al Jazeera had earlier reported 21. [[TAG:warning:toll disputed]]

paragraphs.heading: Ugandans in Russia's army
paragraphs.body: OkayAfrica reported that a letter from Uganda's embassy in Moscow lists 27 Ugandans recruited into Russia's army as dead or presumed dead.

sections.title: US Midterms
sections.summary: Four days out, Democrats lead final polls as Trump swaps two rallies for phone calls

paragraphs.heading: Final stretch
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that Trump canceled weekend rallies in Kansas and Iowa and replaced them with telephone rallies, as Democrats lead the generic ballot by nearly 9 points on average. Newsweek linked the canceled Kansas rally to a poll showing Republican Senator Roger Marshall trailing his Democratic challenger. The final PBS News, NPR and Marist poll found Democrats ahead among likely voters. These are polls, not results. [[TAG:info:vote Nov 3]]
